nodes.label: The Screening Bracket Computation Annex
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Computes every conversion, threshold, target coordinate, exposure time and verdict boundary in advance so that no interpretive step remains between a bench measurement and its verdict; the only unfixed symbol left is what the cell does.

nodes.label: Two-anchor calibration of 2G0 = 177.8 +- 1.6
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: lambda(m) = C exp(-2G0/sqrt(m)) fit twice from anchors sharing no step — the Koonin-Nauenberg watt-scale threshold (176.2) and the measured muonic rate (179.5) — agreeing within 2% across seventy-two orders of magnitude of rate, which satisfies B.2.8 at the instrument level.

nodes.label: The falsifiable fork — line appears or the static map is falsified
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Beam-measured metal screening potentials straddle and exceed m*_det = 4.26, so taken at face value the linear map predicts the 5.49 MeV line is already reachable and thirty-seven years of its absence is itself data. Either branch produces new content; there is no uninformative outcome.

nodes.label: The verdict machine (first-match rules over B F L N H)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Every terminal is reaction, partial with a computed conversion deadline, non-reaction with its bound, or refusal with its cause — nothing is left to interpret, and a neutron excess in the p+d fill is a refusal rather than weak evidence.

nodes.label: Exposure arithmetic and the computed partial-reaction band
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Between ~1e-11 and ~1e-7 W-equivalent the gamma line is decisive within minutes while the 3He inventory route needs months to centuries — so the PARTIAL verdict's band is read off a table rather than judged.

nodes.label: bracket_calculator.py
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Named as the annex's calculator alongside Figure 4 as its instrument; every table in the annex is its output rather than a hand computation.
